clue.text: Fundamental truth college head proclaimed

indicators.note: proclaimed means spoken out, so the title is heard rather than written

parts.note: the head of a college is often styled its principal

explanation.surface: A college head announces some basic truth to the students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proclaimed' signals that the word for a college head is spoken, and its sound gives a different spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle is a basic law or tenet on which reasoning rests.

clue.text: Polytheistic composer missing in centre of China

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so these letters are removed

parts.note: Paganini was an Italian violinist and composer
taken as written

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter

explanation.surface: A composer with many gods goes missing in central China.
explanation.walkthrough: From PAGANINI take IN and I (the middle letter of China), leaving PAGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagan worships many gods rather than one, holding a non-Christian, often polytheistic, faith.

clue.text: Single line about learned man's illustrative effects

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer pieces surround the next one

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, means single
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line
a mage is a learned man or wise man

explanation.surface: A scholar uses a single line for pictorial effect.
explanation.walkthrough: RY is railway, a usual crossword 'line'.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery is vivid descriptive language or pictures creating mental images.

clue.text: Husband leaves like a bounder, knowing this can bite

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: caddish means behaving like a cad or bounder
fly is slang for knowing or shrewd

explanation.surface: A husband walks out like a rotter, aware of the bite that awaits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband leaves' looks like a domestic drama: it takes H out of CADDISH. A bounder is an old British word for a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect is the subject of a cryptic description: something with a possible bite.

clue.text: Scope for enemy to seek advantage by delaying

parts.note: play means scope or room to move
taken as written
time is called the enemy, as in the saying 'time is the enemy'

explanation.surface: The enemy has room to manoeuvre if they stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time, the enemy' is a familiar saying, so enemy gives TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means stalling deliberately to gain an edge, as a team does when ahead late in a match.

clue.text: Initially Mrs Browning's state of decline

indicators.note: initially here means by her initials, so only the first letter of each of her names counts

parts.note: Mrs Browning is the Victorian poet Elizabeth Barrett Browning, wife of Robert Browning
Mrs Browning is the Victorian poet Elizabeth Barrett Browning, wife of Robert Browning
Mrs Browning is the Victorian poet Elizabeth Barrett Browning, wife of Robert Browning

explanation.surface: Mrs Browning's health was already going downhill early on.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Browning is Elizabeth Barrett Browning, the Victorian poet; 'Initially' takes the first letter of each of her three names.
explanation.definitionFit: An ebb is a decline or low point, from the tide flowing out.

clue.text: Leather from chamois is missing, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the remaining letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A leather item made from chamois has gone missing, more's the pity.
explanation.walkthrough: Take IS out of CHAMOIS ('is missing') and rearrange the remaining CHAMO under 'unfortunately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a soft fine leather made from sheepskin or goatskin.

clue.text: Girl out- East embracing old Aborigine

indicators.note: embracing means hugging around, so one piece goes inside
out means away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: Marie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl from out East hugs an elderly native.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out East' drops E from MARIE, and the MARI that remains wraps O. Aborigine here means an original native, the Maori of New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous people of New Zealand, its original inhabitants.

clue.text: Absurd pretence? It's part of the game

definitions.meaning: each acted word or syllable in the parlour guessing game in which players mime clues

explanation.definitionFit: A charade is both an absurd sham and one round of the guessing game played by miming.

clue.text: Time in French city a tinker employed innocently

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Arles is a city in Provence, France
Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker in Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew

explanation.surface: Time spent in a French city by a tinker was put to guileless use.
explanation.walkthrough: SLY is the tinker of The Taming of the Shrew's opening; 'employed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Artlessly means guilelessly or naively, without craft or deceit.

clue.text: Old man getting a thousand a year

parts.note: a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars
p.a. abbreviates per annum, Latin for a year

explanation.surface: An elderly man pockets a thousand pounds annually.
explanation.walkthrough: PA is per annum, a year, as in a salary quoted p.a.
explanation.definitionFit: Old man is informal for one's father or grandfather; grandpa is a familiar word for a grandfather.

clue.text: Cheerful young male worker takes in union leader

indicators.note: takes in means admits within itself, so the following piece goes inside

parts.note: a boy is a young male

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter of union is used

parts.note: an ant is the crossword's stock worker, from the worker ants of a colony

explanation.surface: A happy young worker joins up with the head of a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union leader' looks like a trade-union boss but gives only U, which goes inside BOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Buoyant spirits are high ones, so a buoyant person is upbeat and optimistic.

clue.text: Birthmarks no Scottish girl reveals

parts.note: nae is the Scots form of no
Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet

explanation.surface: A Scottish girl denies having any birthmarks.
explanation.walkthrough: NAE is Scots for 'no'; VI is a short girl's name, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Naevus is the medical term for a mole or birthmark; the plural takes -i.

clue.text: Fortune made stocking a building requisite, mostly

indicators.note: stocking means holding within, as a shop holds goods, so the following pieces go inside

parts.note: fate is fortune or destiny

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a brick is a basic requisite of building

explanation.surface: Someone has made a fortune selling basic building supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocking' puts A and BRIC (the last letter dropped under 'mostly') inside, after the first letter. The definition 'made' is past tense against a base verb, a looseness in the clue as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: To fabricate is to construct or manufacture, the sense in which something is made.

clue.text: Where two parties got engaged at St Albans?

definitions.text: Where two parties got engaged at St Albans?

parts.words: Where two parties got engaged at St Albans?
parts.note: reads like a double betrothal at a cathedral city, but the parties are rival armies; St Albans saw two clashes in the Wars of the Roses

explanation.definitionFit: A site of armed combat, where opposing forces meet in war.

clue.text: Some unspecified area adjoining US city

parts.note: NY is New York, the US city

explanation.surface: An unnamed district borders a big American city.
explanation.walkthrough: NY stands for New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a determiner, the word means some or whichever, without naming which.

clue.text: Primate accepts position, beginning to entertain chosen candidate

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: an ape is a primate
a point is a position or place

indicators.note: beginning to means the very start of the next word, its first letter

explanation.surface: A primate takes up a post and starts entertaining the selected applicant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts the position inside the primate, after its first two letters; 'beginning to' adds the first letter of entertain.
explanation.definitionFit: An appointee is someone selected for a post or office.

clue.text: In favour of race officials, to begin with

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in voting for
starters are the officials who start races

explanation.surface: Someone supports the officials who start a race, at least at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning initially or as a first point, like the first course of a meal.

clue.text: Rising draughtsman found gin with mixer worthwhile

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means going up the page, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a drawer is someone who draws, a draughtsman

indicators.note: a mixer stirs things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming artist found a gin and tonic satisfying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns DRAWER into REWARD; 'with mixer' shuffles GIN to ING. 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rewarding gives satisfaction and repays the effort put in.

clue.text: Cat faces bat in a tree

parts.note: pussy is a familiar word for a cat
cricket bats are made of willow, so the wood stands for the bat

explanation.surface: A cat confronts a bat roosting up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bat' looks like the flying animal, but it is a cricket bat, traditionally made of willow wood.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small willow species with soft furry catkins.

clue.text: Colonist feeding dog with last of offal

indicators.note: feeding means going into, as food goes into a mouth, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A settler gives his dog the last of the offal.
explanation.walkthrough: L, the last letter of offal, goes inside SETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A settler is one who colonises a new land.

clue.text: Catch sight of mole

definitions.meaning: a mole is a secret agent planted inside an organisation

explanation.definitionFit: To glimpse is to catch sight of something; a mole is an undercover agent, another word for which is the answer.

clue.text: Domestic fowl, a pudding ingredient

parts.note: the sultan is a white Turkish breed of domestic chicken

explanation.surface: A farmyard bird serves as one ingredient of a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests chicken in a dessert; SULTAN is a breed of fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Sultanas, dried seedless grapes, go into puddings and cakes.

clue.text: Material inserted-after line is altered

indicators.note: is altered means changed in form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some text was added after a line, and the line changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is altered' reworks the nine letters of the two words before it; 'Material inserted' is the definition, an extra leaf bound into a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An interleaf is an extra page bound between the ordinary leaves of a book.

clue.text: Sail, like Alonso

definitions.meaning: a light sail set above the topgallant on a square-rigged ship
Alonso is the King of Naples in The Tempest, so of a king's rank

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a high square sail, and also means kingly, as Alonso, King of Naples, is.

clue.text: Object of reverence priest displayed in church

indicators.note: displayed in means shown inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: RC is Roman Catholic, a church
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest shows off a venerated object inside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI is the Old Testament priest, a crossword regular; RC is Roman Catholic.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic, such as a saint's bone, is venerated by the faithful.

clue.text: Support the French, having whip-round?

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the outer word goes around the other

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, cat for short
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone backs the French by passing round the hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip-round' suggests a collection; split it: the whip goes round the French article, as 'round' says.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleat is a projecting piece that gives support or a fastening point, as for ropes on a boat.

clue.text: Cry from Jorrocks taking in associate, albeit briefly

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the shortened word wraps round the other piece
briefly means in short form, so the word is cut down to its informal abbreviation

parts.note: albeit means though
an ally is an associate or partner

explanation.surface: A hunting man gives a cry while taking on a companion, however briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: Jorrocks is the fox-hunting grocer in R S Surtees's comic novels. 'albeit, briefly' gives THO, the shortened though, which wraps ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the huntsman's shout on sighting the fox, just what a hunting character would yell.

clue.text: Broad sash in two bits

indicators.note: in means the answer lies inside the next words, running across them

explanation.surface: A wide sash comes in two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the wide sash worn with a Japanese kimono.

clue.text: Move abroad, abandoning good Islamic territory

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: to emigrate is to move abroad to live

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the country, giving up a decent Islamic land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning good' takes G out of EMIGRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir, as in the Gulf.

clue.text: English poet's wretched, returning to join up

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: lorn is a poetic word for forlorn or wretched

explanation.surface: A miserable English poet goes back to sign up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poet's' marks LORN as a literary word; 'returning' reverses it to NROL.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up or enlist, as in joining a course or the forces.

clue.text: Ruffled hotel worker swallows gibe

indicators.note: swallows means takes inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: an inn is a hotel
a dig is a gibe or snide remark
an ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A hotel employee takes an insult without complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' puts the gibe inside the hotel, ahead of the worker; 'Ruffled' looks like a verb but is the adjective definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruffled means upset or irritated, much as an angry person would be.
